payload.overall_summary: The student demonstrated strong interpersonal skills, including respectful engagement, effective questioning, and logical organization of information. However, communication was undermined by a rapid pace, limited use of teach-back to confirm understanding, insufficient collaboration in problem-solving, and inadequate adaptation to the patient's health literacy level. Nonverbal behaviors could not be assessed from the transcript. Overall, the student showed developing competence but requires improvement in patient-centered communication and pacing.

scoring_summary.decision_reason: Fail: total 9/21 is below pass threshold of 11.

criteria.label: Elicits that area around the patienAND other symptoms of tinea (there is cracking, redness and peeling of skin between toes) (i.e. when asked to describe symptoms)
criteria.reason: The student asks to describe symptoms but does not elicit specific details about cracking, redness, or peeling skin between toes as required; the patient only mentions flaking and itchiness.

criteria.label: Elicits that symptoms started three weeks ago after working on the farm wearing boots all day (i.e. when asked when it started)
criteria.reason: The student asks about duration but the patient's response is vague ('after a long hard working day in the form') and does not specify three weeks ago or farm work with boots; no clarification sought.

criteria.label: Elicits the patient has not had the symptoms before AND has not tried anything for symptoms yet AND has no signs of infection (no pus, swelling etc.)
criteria.reason: While the student asks if condition occurred prior and patient says 'No', and later asks if tried anything and patient says 'No', the student does not explicitly elicit absence of infection signs (no pus, swelling etc.).

criteria.label: Advises patient has tinea OR fungal infection on the skin OR cause of itchiness due to wearing boots whole day (hot and humid)
criteria.reason: The student states 'I believe that you're currently experiencing tinnia' but mispronounces it and links cause vaguely to 'your work' without specifying wearing boots whole day in hot/humid conditions; does not clearly advise fungal infection or exact cause per rubric.

criteria.label: Recommends any of ONE the following topical therapy: Terbinafine, OR Miconazole/ clotrimazole/ econazole/ bifonazole/ ketoconazole, OR Combination hydrocortisone/antifungal
criteria.reason: The student recommends 'lima fine' (likely misheard terbinafine) but calls it '1% cream' and applies twice daily, which is incorrect for terbinafine (should be once daily); this misrepresents the therapy and does not correctly recommend any listed option per regimen.

criteria.label: Counsels on how to use chosen product in Point 5: - Terbinafine: Apply a thin layer once daily for 1 week - Miconazole: Apply a thin layer twice daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Clotrimazole/Econazole: Apply a thin layer 2 or 3 times a day; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Bifonazole: Apply a thin layer once daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Ketoconazole: Apply a thin layer 1 or 2 times daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Combination hydrocortisone/antifungal (available combinations are clotrimazole + hydrocortisone OR miconazole + hydrocortisone): Apply a thin layer 2 times a day for one week then continue with antifungal only
criteria.reason: Counsels to apply 'lima fine' twice daily for 1 week, which does not match any correct regimen: terbinafine should be once daily, and antifungals like miconazole require continuation after resolution; advice is inaccurate per rubric details.

criteria.label: Recommends at least ONE of the following future preventive action: maintain good foot hygiene; keep feet clean and dry especially after working at the farm; avoid sharing towels/footwear; use antifungal (or non-medicated) powder in shoes to reduce moisture; wear open-toed footwear; use cotton (non-synthetic) socks; wear shoes that have breathable material (such as leather); place shoes in the sun to dry if it get damp; discard old shoes that may have a high density of fungal spores
criteria.reason: The student advises to 'try to wear more breathable material shoes' and 'make sure your feet are constantly clean and try to dry your feet with a different towel', covering breathable materials and foot hygiene/dryness as preventive actions.

criteria.label: Advises the patient to see their doctor /pharmacist if their symptoms do not improve or worsens
criteria.reason: The student says 'if your symptoms persist or your condition worsens... you may immediately seek general prediction to get your condition moderately checked by a doctor', which conveys the intent to seek care if worsening, but phrasing is non-standard ('general prediction', 'moderately checked') and does not clearly advise seeing doctor/pharmacist per rubric; advice is inadequately expressed.

keep_start_stop.keep: Continue to initiate the consultation politely and ask open-ended questions about symptoms and history, as this builds rapport and gathers essential information effectively.
keep_start_stop.start: Begin using precise medical terminology (e.g., 'tinea pedis' not 'tinnia') and explicitly link clinical findings to causative factors like prolonged boot use in warm conditions to demonstrate diagnostic accuracy.
keep_start_stop.stop: Avoid providing incorrect dosing instructions or misstating medication regimens; always verify recommended usage details (frequency, duration) against standard guidelines before advising the patient.

payload.overall_summary: The student demonstrated basic consultation skills by initiating dialogue and gathering some history but failed to meet key rubric criteria due to incomplete symptom elicitation, inaccurate diagnosis linkage, incorrect therapeutic recommendations, and poor follow-up advice. Critical errors in advising the condition and recommending therapy were not compensated by partial success in preventive counseling, resulting in an unsatisfactory performance requiring significant improvement in clinical accuracy and communication precision.
